article_title: Role-playing monument exploration: an online educational game with a role-playing mechanism and multi-dimensional scaffolding for monument tours
citation: Shu-Wei Liu, Hung-Yu Chan, & Huei-Tse Hou. (2025). Role-playing monument exploration: an online educational game with a role-playing mechanism and multi-dimensional scaffolding for monument tours. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10480-3
title: 1946 Base Exploration: a Gather Town role-playing game-based monument guide with multi-dimensional scaffolding
description: An online educational game built in Gather Town that reconstructs a real military monument in northern Taiwan, in which three-learner teams role-play 1946 officers completing three timed mission stages (arranging facilities, planning guard paths, determining attack location) with guides playing the commander, soldiers, and invaders. The article states it was built "using Gather Town as the main game platform to construct an authentic virtual space based on the topography and appearance of a real military monument in northern Taiwan". Learners draw solutions on an in-game whiteboard and receive merits-based scoring for task correctness, communication attitude, and alertness to invaders.
requirements: Guides who role-play historical characters and provide dynamic scaffolding during play
An authentic virtual space based on the monument's real topography and appearance
constraints: The study used a single military monument in northern Taiwan with teams of three learners
target_learners: adult learners aged 20–55 in online monument guide activities
target_learning_goals: history and background of military monuments
application of military strategies (attacking directions and guarding routes)
examples: In the quasi-experiment, the experimental group explored the base in Gather Town for 60 minutes while guides played the commander, soldier, and invaders
